title: A DOOR OPEN TO THE POOR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If the offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, you are to offer a dove or a young pigeon. The priest shall bring it to the altar, wring off the head and burn it on the altar; its blood shall be drained out on the side of the altar.'" - Lev 1:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God comes down one final step. From bulls, to sheep, to birds — a dove or a pigeon, which even the poorest Israelite could catch or buy for almost nothing.

And notice something tender: with the bird, the priest does the killing. The bird is too small and delicate for the worshipper's hands. God accommodated even that.

This provision was not theoretical. Read Luke 2:24. When Mary and Joseph brought the infant Jesus to the temple, they offered a pair of doves — the sacrifice of the poor, spelled out in Leviticus 12:8. The Son of God was born into a family that could not afford a lamb.

Sit with that. The King of glory entered the world through the door marked "for those who cannot afford much." He knows what it is to be counted among the ones with little. Though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor (2 Cor 8:9).

If you have ever felt that your resources, your abilities, or your circumstances put God's presence out of your reach, Leviticus 1 has been steadily dismantling that fear for fourteen verses. The altar is not gated by wealth. It never was.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God is equally accessible to me regardless of what I can afford to give?
2. How does it change my view of Jesus to know He was born into poverty?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You made a way for the poorest to come, and that Your own Son came that way. Nothing about my circumstances shuts me out from You. Amen.
